To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-23T09:12:00Z
Subject: SLO observability & temporary dashboard access request — Solstice.ai

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for the productive demo last week. Procurement at Solstice (copied here: procurement@solstice.ai) has a short checklist to complete our vendor evaluation: we need a concise description of how Redwood measures availability and p95 latency for the text-generation endpoints, a sample of historical metric slices (7 days), and short-term read-only access to a dashboard so our SREs can validate the instrumentation.

To be explicit: we are not asking for long-term live access or raw logs — just a time-boxed read-only dashboard (48 hours) and a one-off evidence packet (PDF) showing SLO calculation, alerting thresholds, and recent incidents if any.

Can you point me to who handles temporary access and whether Redwood has a standard process for these procurement visibility requests? We have a target procurement cutover for June.

Thanks,
Alice Wong
Procurement Lead | Solstice.ai
attachments: none

From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai

Karthik / Monica — FYI we got Solstice's procurement note. They want: 1) short description of how we measure availability & p95 latency; 2) 7-day metric slice; 3) 48-hour read-only dashboard access for their SREs.

Questions: do we have a pre-approved template/process for granting time-limited dashboard views to prospects? Monica, can you confirm whether this is permissible under our telemetry exposure policy and what redactions (if any) we require? Karthik, I think we can offer a scoped Grafana view + a packaged PDF (SLO_evidence_packet) — do you want to add the alert playbook bit?

I'd like to keep this tight: access window = 48 hours, view = per-route SLO summary (no request bodies, no raw request ids), and explicit audit log of who looked at it. Also propose we require an NDA or a click-through procurement acknowledgement before enabling access.

If we can move fast, I'll offer the access window for the week of May 25. Thoughts?

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-23T11:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLO observability & temporary dashboard access request — Solstice.ai

Agree with the constraints. A few concrete proposals:

- Evidence packet: SLO definition (availability = successful 200 responses / total requests per route), p95 latency computation details (client-observed vs. server-side timing), sampling windows, and recent rolling counts. We'll include a short incidents timeline if applicable.
- Dashboard: create a read-only Grafana snapshot with the following panels only: per-route availability (1m, 5m), p95 latency, error-rate, and a synthetic check overlay for regional routing. No trace links, no request-level identifiers.
- Access guardrails: time-limited link (48h), IP allowlist option, and audit logging (user email + access timestamps). We'll also redact internal hostnames and any customer identifiers in the metrics.
- Approvals: require procurement acknowledgement (we can use the standard procurement click-through: "I confirm I will not attempt to exfiltrate raw telemetry") — legal has been OK in previous cases.

I'll package the SLO_evidence_packet.pdf and short access_instructions.txt. Monica — can you take point on the redaction checklist and confirm whether we need a short SOC2-procurement exception note?

Karthik
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-23T11:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLO observability & temporary dashboard access request — Solstice.ai

Nikhil / Karthik — quick note: Legal asked that we include a one-paragraph statement referencing our telemetry handling and a pointer to the SOC2 report (we will not hand over SOC2 contents, but we can point to the public attestations). We'll also add an explicit line in the access_instructions.txt about scope and the audit trail. No additional redactions expected beyond removing internal hostnames and any PII.

I can review the packet and sign off on the redaction checklist by EOD. Once approved, I'll coordinate with infra to generate the read-only snapshot link and set the 48-hour TTL.

Monica Patel
Technical Program Manager, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
To: Alice Wong <alice@solstice.ai>, procurement@solstice.ai, ops+platform@solstice.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-23T13:45:00Z
Subject: Re: SLO observability & temporary dashboard access request — Solstice.ai

Hi Alice — thanks, and glad procurement is moving this along. We can accommodate a limited, time-boxed view for your SREs. Below is the plan and next steps: 

1) What we'll provide (48-hour window):
   - Read-only Grafana snapshot (per-route availability, p95 latency, error-rate, synthetic overlay) — link will be a TTL-ed, tokenized URL.
   - SLO_evidence_packet.pdf (attached): definition of availability and p95 latency, sampling windows, alert thresholds, and a short incidents timeline for the last 30 days.
   - access_instructions.txt (attached): simple steps, scope, and required procurement click-through acknowledgement.

2) Guardrails:
   - No request-level traces, no raw logs, and no customer identifiers will be exposed.
   - Access will be logged (user email + IP + timestamps) and retained per our telemetry access policy.
   - TTL = 48 hours from activation. We can optionally IP-restrict if you provide a CIDR.

3) Required step to proceed:
   - Please confirm acceptance of the procurement acknowledgement in the access_instructions.txt (short checkbox). Once we receive confirmation, we'll schedule activation for a 48-hour window.

4) Timeline: if you confirm by EOD 2026-05-24, we can enable the view on May 26 and keep it open for 48 hours.

Attachments: SLO_evidence_packet.pdf (summary), access_instructions.txt, grafana-temporary-link.txt (will include the TTL-ed URL once the link is generated).

Let me know if you prefer an IP allowlist or want us to coordinate a short joint session where our SREs walk your team through the panels.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
